prompt: Create ONE seamless square BASE-COLOR MATERIAL texture for the slate roofs of a native 3D woodland fantasy village. Two actual reference images are attached: the existing slate material and the USER'S APPROVED CHAPEL GAMEPLAY REFERENCE. Use the gameplay reference as the color and mood authority; the existing tile is only the shared roof-family construction reference. The existing material renders too pale and reads as broad grey corrugated bands. Replace that with the reference chapel's distinctly deep charcoal BLUE-GREY slate, with legible individual staggered tiles. Mature, restrained STYLIZED PAINTERLY fantasy in the visual genre of Diablo Immortal, natural subdued colors, never a photograph, cute toy or pastel. Output 1024 by 1024 pixels. FLAT FRONT-ON ORTHOGRAPHIC color material only: NO roof object, building, perspective, isometric view, environment, foliage, UI, borders, labels or gutters. Physical repeat is 2.6 by 2.6 metres, exactly EIGHT straight horizontal courses, each course 0.325m high. Around six tiles across a course, mostly rectangular thin natural slate tiles 0.38-0.5m wide; stagger the vertical joints by about half a tile on alternating rows. Maintain clear, narrow but readable dark vertical joint lines and quiet edge chips to distinguish individual pieces on mobile. Rich deep low-saturation blue-grey and charcoal with subtle blue-green mineral variation; keep the overall material darker and bluer than the existing grey tile, with no saturated blue or cyan. Broad clean slate faces and delicate fine grain, few hairline irregularities and restrained chipped corners. Do not add large pale white veins, marble cracks, moss, bright mottling or grunge. Uniform neutral diffuse illumination across the entire sheet. NO baked directional light, no highlights, no glossy glints, no cast shadows, no large BLACK HORIZONTAL SHADOW BANDS beneath each row: actual 3D overlapping tile geometry and the game lights will make their own relief. Joints may have subtly darker material color, but avoid painted 3D bevel lighting. Flat tileable albedo, not a normal map or roughness map. Opposite edges must repeat coherently, including the staggered course layout. Design for the blue slate to contrast naturally against the same-family warm grey limestone and aged oak.
